1.web: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved. Beloved
1.asv: I am come into my garden, my sister, my bride: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends; Drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

2.web: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
2.asv: I was asleep, but my heart waked: It is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; For my head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.

3.web: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?
3.asv: I have put off my garment; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

4.web: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
4.asv: My beloved put in his hand by the holeof the door, And my heart was moved for him.

5.web: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
5.asv: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands dropped with myrrh, And my fingers with liquid myrrh, Upon the handles of the bolt.

6.web: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left; and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.
6.asv: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone. My soul had failed me when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

7.web: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.
7.asv: The watchmen that go about the city found me, They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my mantle from me.

8.web: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love. Friends
8.asv: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, That ye tell him, that I am sick from love.

9.web: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us? Beloved
9.asv: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than another beloved, That thou dost so adjure us?

10.web: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
10.asv: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.

11.web: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
11.asv: His head isasthe most fine gold; His locks are bushy, and black as a raven.

12.web: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
12.asv: His eyes are like doves beside the water-brooks, Washed with milk, and fitly set.

13.web: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
13.asv: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, Asbanks of sweet herbs: His lips are as lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

14.web: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
14.asv: His hands areasrings of gold set with beryl: His body isasivory work overlaid with sapphires.

15.web: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
15.asv: His legs areaspillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: His aspect is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

16.web: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
16.asv: His mouth is most sweet; Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
